pictures.scene: Guercino, King David — the king seated in his crown and ermine with the gold mantle over his rose-red robe, the sceptre held down in one hand and the other laid on a stone tablet cut with a line of the psalms, his head turned away, for the choirmaster a Psalm of David, how long O LORD
pictures.name: pd_guercino_king_david

pictures.scene: Aert van der Neer, River View by Moonlight — the small moon alone in a covered sky, laying one thin track of light on the wide river, the windmill and the sailing barges standing black against it and a carter waiting on the dark bank, will You forget me forever, how long will You hide Your face from me
pictures.name: pd_van_der_neer_river_view_by_moonlight

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Sorrowing Old Man — the old man in blue working clothes doubled over on a wooden chair by the fire with both fists pressed into his eyes, how long must I wrestle in my soul, with sorrow in my heart each day
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_sorrowing_old_man

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Saul and David — the young David in his red striped tunic and gold-embroidered sleeve bent over the harp in the dark, both hands on the strings and his eyes lowered, playing before the king who hunts him, how long will my enemy dominate me, consider me and respond O LORD my God
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_saul_and_david

pictures.scene: William Holman Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ standing in the night garden in His white robe and jewelled clasp, the crown of thorns on His head and the halo behind it, raising His hand to the overgrown door while the lit lantern hangs burning from His other hand, give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Christ Mocked — Christ standing quiet in the middle with the crown of thorns being lowered onto His head, four tormentors pressed in around Him, one in a green turban laying a mailed hand on His shoulder and another with oak leaves in his cap leaning in at His ear, lest my enemy say I have overcome him, and my foes rejoice when I fall
pictures.name: pd_bosch_christ_mocked

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Woman before the Rising Sun — a woman standing alone on the dark heath with her back to us and both hands opened out at her sides, the low hills before her and the whole sky going gold above them, but I have trusted in Your loving devotion, my heart will rejoice in Your salvation
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_woman_rising_sun

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Singing Angels — eight angels in jewelled circlets and heavy red and gold brocade crowded around the carved wooden lectern, all of them open-mouthed in song over the book, I will sing to the LORD, for He has been good to me
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_singing_angels

lines.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
How long will You hide Your face from me?
How long must I wrestle in my soul,
with sorrow in my heart each day?
How long will my enemy dominate me?
Consider me and respond, O LORD my God.
lest my enemy say, “I have overcome him,”
and my foes rejoice when I fall.
But I have trusted in Your loving devotion;
my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD,
for He has been good to me.
